approval.decision: Kris approved variant 1, "Count and failure marks", for how a Story Save refusal shows several failing drafts: screen story-save-refusal / marked, revision marked-v1. Variants 2 (stepper-v1) and 3 (first-v1) are not approved. The decision is recorded in issue #114 (comment 6820468198).
behaviour: Save checks every beat draft. If any fails, it writes none of them, keeps all drafts and opens the first failing draft in project order with its error.

The header status reads "Nothing saved. 3 of 5 drafts need changes:" (the numbers are the live counts), followed by one link per scene with its failure count. A link opens that scene's first failing draft.
Failing beats get a red ! and a red top edge in Tracks, with the reason in Reel and the tooltip. Ready drafts keep the amber •. The scene menu lists draft and failure counts per scene.
Each failing beat shows its error when selected. Commit on a failing draft shows that draft's error.
The count and marks update as the author fixes drafts. When none fail, the status reads "5 unsaved beat drafts. Ready to save."
Marks appear only after a refused Save, never while the author types a first draft.
A source conflict uses the approved B editor from story-draft-conflict (compact-v2). A new dialogue beat with no speaker shows "Choose a speaker." An unclosed text tag shows "Close {i} with {/i}."
deviations: Fictional browser-memory mock. It has no source transaction, history, stale-revision refresh, busy lock or Flush. The text-tag check covers only paired tags. The scene menu stands in for Combined v1's scene tree.
Only the beats that carry drafts are editable. Branch path and non-text beats are context.
The recorded source predates the Brass and slate palette (#150). The lab still pins this version; production colours follow docs/UI.md.
The toolbar still reads "Save refusal study · unapproved" in the reviewed source. The approval record owns the design status; that string is prototype scaffolding.
Variants 2 and 3 remain in the lab as unapproved drafts for comparison.
